room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "FAHM": a woman proudly holds up a big snapshot of her whole FAM: kids, grandma and the dog: FAHM = FAM
note: Also wife (ma femme = my wife).

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "mah-DAHM": a grand MADAM in pearls rings the brass bell on the reception desk to greet the visitors: mah-DAHM = MADAM
note: The polite way to address or name any adult woman: Mrs, ma'am (Madame Dupont, Bonjour madame).

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "mah-duh-mwah-ZEHL": a young miss with a basket of red roses blows a big "MWAH!" kiss to SELL one more rose: mah-duh-MWAH-ZEHL = MWAH + SELL
note: Old-fashioned on forms: official French now uses madame for every woman; still heard as a polite address to a girl or young woman.

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "DAHM": an elegant lady with a lace parasol steps around the little beaver DAM built across the hall fountain: DAHM = DAM
note: Also the queen in chess and cards; le jeu de dames = checkers.

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "pehr-SON": a PERSON carries her little SON high on her shoulders so he can see the portraits: pehr-SON = PER-SON
note: Always feminine, even for a man (cette personne est gentille); ne ... personne = nobody.

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "proh-pree-yay-TEHR": the proud PROPRIETOR of the gallery jingles a giant ring of old brass keys in welcome: proh-pree-yay-TEHR = PROPRIETOR
note: Also the landlord or landlady of a rented home.

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "OM": a bearded MAN sits cross-legged on a cushion under the stairs chanting "OM": OM = OM
note: Also mankind (l'homme = humanity) and, with an adjective, a man of a kind (un homme d'affaires = a businessman).

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "muh-SYEUH": a gentleman in a white suit and top hat finds blue paint splattered all down his jacket: how MESSY, sir!: muh-SYEUH = MESSY-uh
note: The polite way to address or name any man: Mr, sir (Monsieur Martin, Bonjour monsieur).

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "GAH": a young guy in overalls cries "GAH!" as his tower of parcels wobbles: GAH = GAH!
note: Familiar: guy, lad (un gars sympa = a nice guy).

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "seh-NYUHR": a SENIOR lord with a white beard, a velvet cape and a cane comes slowly down the grand staircase: seh-NYUHR = SENIOR
note: Historical: the lord of a manor; in church language le Seigneur = the Lord.

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "ZHAHN": a cheerful group of people with picnic baskets and walking sticks sets off on a JAUNT: ZHAHN = JAUN(t)
note: Always plural: les gens = people (beaucoup de gens).

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
hook: "vwah-ZAN": the next-door neighbor brings a VASE IN, full of sunflowers: vwah-ZAN = VASE-IN
note: Also as an adjective: neighboring, next-door (le village voisin).

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "VEE": a grandma lifts a toddler to watch a V of geese fly past the glass: LIFE goes on: VEE = V
note: Also a living or livelihood (gagner sa vie = to earn a living) and a lifetime (pour la vie = for life).

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "zhuh-NEHS": a young girl zooms across the tiles on a skateboard hugging a green Loch NESS monster toy, full of YOUTH: zhuh-NEHS = ...NESS(ie)
note: Also young people as a group (la jeunesse d'aujourd'hui = young people today).

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "FOOL": a whole crowd of cousins in silly jester hats squeezes in at the back for the photo: a crowd of FOOLs: FOOL = FOOL
note: Une foule de = loads of (une foule d'idées).

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "ahn-FAHN": a CHILD bounces up and down ON a big orange hopper ball, just for FUN: ahn-FAHN = ON FUN
note: Also a son or daughter of any age (nos enfants = our children); un enfant / une enfant.

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "ah-DEWLT": a toddler wears his dad's huge suit and tie, trying hard to look like an ADULT: ah-DEWLT = ADULT
note: Also an adjective: adult, grown-up (l'âge adulte = adulthood).

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "gahr-SOHN": a little boy in a tall black guard's helmet stands GUARD by his dad: the GUARD SON: gahr-SOHN = GUARD SON
note: Old-fashioned for a café waiter; calling "Garçon!" to a waiter is rude today.

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "AHZH": grandpa takes a deep breath to blow out a cake bristling with candles: what an AGE!: AHZH = AGE
note: Quel âge as-tu ? = how old are you?; le Moyen Âge = the Middle Ages.

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "ah-bee-TAHN": a sun-TANned farmer from the village has A BEE perched on his straw hat: ah-bee-TAHN = A BEE TAN
note: Also a resident; les habitants = the locals, the population (5 000 habitants).

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "gah-MAN": a cheeky kid in a cap zooms past on a scooter while his pal cheers "GO, MAN!": gah-MAN ≈ GO, MAN!
note: Familiar: kid (une gamine); as an adjective it can mean childish.

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "EHTR": a small friendly glowing being from the stars waves its stubby arms over A TRAY of lemonade: EHTR ≈ (a) TRAY
note: Also the verb être = to be; un être humain = a human being.

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "PEUHPL": a great PURPLE tapestry shows a whole PEOPLE marching together with blank banners: PEUHPL ≈ PURPLE
note: A people or nation (le peuple français); also the common people, as opposed to the rulers.

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "an-dee-vee-DEW": in a row of identical grey toy penguins on the shelf, one INDIVIDUAL wears a red scarf and waves: an-dee-vee-DEW = INDIVIDU(al)
note: Often mildly negative in news and police talk: un individu = a suspicious person, 'an individual'.

room_name: La salle des âges · The hall of ages
hook: "ah-doh-lay-SAHN": a gangly ADOLESCENT with big headphones sprawls on a beanbag and rolls his eyes at the photo: ah-doh-lay-SAHN = ADOLESCENT
note: Short familiar form: un ado.

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "mee-NYOHN": a cute kitten curls up in a basket of ONIONS and the painter coos "my ONION!": mee-NYOHN ≈ my ONION
note: Also sweet, kind (c'est mignon de ta part = that's sweet of you).

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "ah-doh-RAHBL": an ADORABLE baby bunny peeks round A DOOR in a painted cardboard house: ah-doh-RAHBL ≈ A DOOR-ABLE
note: Same as English.

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "fah-tee-GAY": a worn-out painter in a smock snores on his stool, brush drooping: total FATIGUE: fah-tee-GAY ≈ FATIGUE
note: Also worn (des chaussures fatiguées = worn-out shoes).

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "zhoh-LEE": a JOLLY grandma poses on a chair with a pretty bunch of white LILIES: zhoh-LEE ≈ JOLLY
note: Ironic too: c'est du joli! = that's a fine mess!

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "mah-nyee-FEEK": a mouse peers up through a giant MAGNIFYING glass at its own splendid whiskers: "EEK!": mah-nyee-FEEK ≈ MAGNIFY-EEK
note: Strong praise: superb, magnificent (un temps magnifique = gorgeous weather).

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "GRAH": a seagull swoops through the skylight squawking "GRAH!" and grabs a greasy slice of pizza: GRAH ≈ GRAH! (a seagull squawk)
note: Of food: fatty, greasy (le beurre est gras); en gras = in bold type. Calling a person gras is rude; gros is the usual word.

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "say-LEHBR": a famous singer bows on the posing platform while fans CELEBRATE with confetti: a real CELEB: say-LEHBR ≈ CELEB(rate)
note: Famous, well-known (un tableau célèbre = a famous painting).

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "BLOHN": a hairdresser's hairdryer has BLOWN a posing lion's blond mane into a huge fluffy cloud: BLOHN ≈ BLOWN
note: Feminine blonde (une fille blonde); also pale gold in general: le sable blond = golden sand.

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "VEEF": a lively puppy dashes across the floorboards with a big BEEF bone in its jaws: VEEF ≈ BEEF
note: Also bright or vivid (rouge vif = bright red), quick-witted; de vive voix = in person.

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "pehr-DEW": a PAIR of lost ducklings huddle under a fern still wet with DEW, peeping for mom: pehr-DEW ≈ PAIR + DEW
note: Also wasted (du temps perdu = wasted time) and done for (je suis perdu = I'm done for).

room_name: L'atelier des portraits · The portrait studio
hook: "proh-FEEL": a young PRO with a real FEEL for faces paints a black side-view profile on his canvas: proh-FEEL ≈ PRO FEEL
note: Also an online or job profile (le profil du poste = the job profile).

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "ah-tee-TEWD": a girl crosses her arms and sticks her nose in the air: what an ATTITUDE!: ah-tee-TEWD ≈ ATTITUDE
note: Also a stance or position (l'attitude du gouvernement) and a ballet pose.

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "kohn-TAHN": a man with a deep TAN happily licks a big ice-cream CONE, totally content: kohn-TAHN ≈ CONE + TAN
note: Content de = pleased with (je suis content de toi). Not 'the content' (= le contenu).

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "ew-MAN": a little tin robot points at a boy and beeps "YOU, MAN... HUMAN!": ew-MAN ≈ YOU, MAN
note: Also humane, kind (un traitement humain).

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "pran-see-PAHL": a little PRINCE in a paper crown and his PAL squeeze into the main armchair: pran-see-PAHL ≈ PRINCE + PAL
note: Main, chief (la rue principale = the main street); le principal = the main thing, or a school principal.

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "FYEHR": a proud peacock fans its tail in front of the crackling FIRE: FYEHR ≈ FIRE
note: Can mean haughty; se fier à = to trust (a different verb).

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "ehg-ZAHKT": a hen sits by her EGG SACK and counts every egg twice, exactly: ehg-ZAHKT ≈ EGG SACK
note: Also correct, accurate (c'est exact = that's right).

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "ew-NEEK": on the mantel, one UNIQUE zebra with polka dots stands among striped ones: ew-NEEK ≈ UNIQUE
note: Also only: un fils unique = an only son, une rue à sens unique = a one-way street.

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "pehr-soh-NEHL": NELL hugs her padlocked diary to her chest: PERSON-NELL, private!: pehr-soh-NEHL ≈ PERSON-NELL
note: Le personnel (noun) = the staff, personnel.

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "shahr-MAHN": a CHARM-MAN in a bow tie bows and kisses a granny's hand: shahr-MAHN ≈ CHARM-MAN
note: Prince charmant = Prince Charming.

room_name: Le salon des caractères · The character parlor
hook: "zhah-LOO": a pug gives the goldfish JAR a jealous LOOK as everyone admires the fish: zhah-LOO ≈ JAR + LOO(k)
note: Jaloux de = jealous of; also protective (jaloux de sa liberté).

room_name: La salle du courage · The courage gym
change: added (second room of planned room R_character_01)
hook: "BRAHV": a tiny hamster stands up to a big barking dog while the crowd yells "BRAVO!": BRAHV ≈ BRAV(o)
note: Before the noun it means good, decent (un brave homme = a decent man).

room_name: La salle du courage · The courage gym
change: added (second room of planned room R_character_01)
hook: "tee-MEED": a TIMID rabbit hides behind a big TEA pot on the bench: tee-MEED ≈ TEA + (ti)MID
note: Shy, bashful.

room_name: La salle du courage · The courage gym
change: added (second room of planned room R_character_01)
hook: "san-pah-TEEK": a nice koala PATs every runner and passes a TEAK tray of cookies: san-pah-TEEK ≈ (san-)PAT-TEAK
note: False friend: means nice, friendly (short: sympa); sympathetic = compatissant.

room_name: La salle du courage · The courage gym
change: added (second room of planned room R_character_01)
hook: "an-day-pahn-DAHN": a toddler wearing a shiny PENDANT climbs the rope ladder all by herself: in-de-PENDANT: an-day-pahn-DAHN ≈ (in)de-PENDANT
note: Also self-employed (travailleur indépendant), and of a country: independent.

room_name: La salle du courage · The courage gym
change: added (second room of planned room R_character_01)
hook: "koo-rah-ZHEUH": a dove shouts "COO! RAH!" and leaps off the high box into the foam pit: koo-rah-ZHEUH ≈ COO-RAH!
note: Brave, daring (courageuse in the feminine).

room_name: La salle du courage · The courage gym
hook: "fay-mee-NAN": NAN, in a frilly pink leotard, twirls a long ribbon on the mat with FEMININE grace: fay-mee-NAN ≈ FEMININE (NAN)
note: Also female (le sexe féminin) and grammatical gender: un nom féminin = a feminine noun.
